drhp.business: Aequs is a precision components manufacturer with fully vertically integrated capabilities (machining, forging, surface treatment, assembly) primarily serving the Aerospace Segment, and also a Consumer Segment covering consumer electronics, plastics and consumer durables. It supplies global OEMs and system integrators from three engineering-led manufacturing ecosystems in India plus dedicated facilities in France and the U.S.

drhp.mdna: Aerospace Segment mix rising (89.19% of FY25 revenue) with materially higher margins than loss-making Consumer Segment|Move up value chain to 5-axis machining and higher value engine/landing components to improve margins|Increasing domestic raw-material procurement to reduce raw material costs and improve margins|Asset-light model via leasing buildings from Group Companies|Moderate capacity utilization (41.77% FY25) leaving room to scale without major fixed cost

internal_operational.detail: A significant portion of net external revenue is derived from the Aerospace Segment; any decrease in demand or reduced economic benefit from aerospace products may adversely affect the business. Heavily dependent on the global aerospace industry, particularly the U.S., France and India.
internal_operational.evidence: Net external revenue - Aerospace Segment as % of revenue from operations: 88.23% (H1 FY26), 86.00% (H1 FY25), 89.19% (FY2025), 78.44% (FY2024), 72.06% (FY2023); amounts ₹4,739.53M, ₹3,947.23M, ₹8,246.41M, ₹7,569.78M, ₹5,851.82M
internal_operational.title: Revenue concentration in Aerospace Segment

internal_operational.detail: Heavily dependent on ten largest customer groups (primarily OEMs in aerospace and consumer). Loss of any, or adverse change in their financial condition, would adversely affect operations. Revenue from Hasbro declined between FY2023 and FY2024. Named customers include Collins, Eaton and Hasbro.
internal_operational.title: Dependence on ten largest customer groups

internal_operational.detail: Contractual arrangements with OEM customer groups are requirement-based and do not obligate customers to place fixed quantities; orders are via purchase orders that may be amended or cancelled prior to finalization, risking inventory/supply-schedule mismatch.
internal_operational.evidence: 15 OEM customer groups serviced globally as of September 30, 2025; average relationship with 10 largest customer groups is 11 years
internal_operational.title: Requirement-based OEM contracts with no fixed order commitment

strategy_growth.detail: Growth strategies (increasing wallet share, moving up the value chain, diversifying aerospace customers, growing consumer portfolio) require additional capital; may be unable to sustain historical growth. Revenue declined in FY2025.
strategy_growth.title: Inability to execute business plan and growth strategies

strategy_growth.detail: Significant revenue from direct and indirect exports across 22 international markets; exposed to export tariffs (including recent U.S. tariffs on Indian exports), multiple tax/cost structures, and foreign-law risks (e.g., AAF anti-competitive clause exposure; French Monetary Code approval for >25% control change).
strategy_growth.evidence: India sales only 11.44% (H1 FY26), 10.74% (FY2025), 12.67% (FY2024), 11.67% (FY2023) of revenue; largest markets USA 23.02% and France 22.11% (FY2025); sells in 22 international markets
strategy_growth.title: Export dependence and international business risks

strategy_growth.detail: Subject to sector-wide threats: high capital investment, operational complexity, smaller batch sizes, higher precision requirements, technological obsolescence, cybersecurity, policy/infrastructure constraints, fluctuating global demand, competition, raw material price volatility, skill shortages and compliance costs.
strategy_growth.evidence: Raw materials (steel, titanium, alloys, composites) subject to significant price fluctuations; skilled-labour shortage in robotics/automation/advanced machining
strategy_growth.title: Manufacturing sector threats and challenges (India PEC sector)

High revenue concentration in the Aerospace Segment (89.19% of FY25 revenue) and in the ten largest customer groups (88.57% of FY25 revenue; top five 73.17%).
Consumer Segment structurally loss-making (segment EBITDA margin -28.68% FY25) and shrinking (net external revenue fell from Rs 2,269.50M FY23 to Rs 999.65M FY25).
Revenue declined 4.19% in FY25; goodwill impairment of Rs 482.65M booked in FY25; multiple subsidiaries loss-making with one (ATHPL) approved for winding up.

Leverage and off-balance-sheet exposure: net debt/equity 0.99x FY25; Company + Individual Promoter guarantees ~Rs 5,473.74M / Rs 5,422.74M; 39.90% of borrowings in unhedged foreign currency; contingent liabilities Rs 934.32M (~117% of net worth per domains).

Emphasis of matter in the auditor's report for FY24 and FY23 (subsidiary guarantee/FEMA and unsettled foreign-currency payables); untraceable historical corporate/RoC records relied on a PCS search report.
Company's own additional machinery orders (Offer-funded capex) not yet placed; portion of proceeds earmarked for unidentified acquisitions (inorganic + GCP capped at 35% of Offer + Pre-IPO).

parameter_scores.basis: Loss for the year in all reported periods (FY25 Rs 1,023.46M); negative PAT margin and negative RoNW (-14.47% FY25); FY25 goodwill impairment Rs 482.65M.
Revenue declined 4.19% in FY25 (Rs 9,246.06M) after +18.83% FY24, but H1FY26 rebounded +17.03% to Rs 5,371.59M.
Aerospace 89.19% of FY25 revenue; top 10 customer groups 88.57%; top 5 73.17% — high dependence on a narrow base.
Net debt/equity 0.99x FY25; large Company and Promoter guarantees (~Rs 5,473.74M / Rs 5,422.74M); 39.90% forex borrowings unhedged; contingent liabilities ~117% of net worth.
Only fully vertically integrated aerospace precision manufacturer in a single SEZ in India per F&S; Tier-1 status with Airbus/Boeing; high entry barriers and long customer tenures.

Board 6 with 3 independents; but emphasis of matter FY24/FY23, untraceable historical records, extensive related-party transactions (Rs 2,540.41M FY25), and most directors lacking listed-company experience.
Consolidated operating cash flow volatile and negative in some periods (H1FY25 Rs -117.27M, FY24 Rs -191.08M) with multiple subsidiaries reporting negative operating cash flows.
Objects concrete (debt repayment Rs 4,331.67M, machinery capex Rs 640.02M) but Company's own machinery orders not yet placed and a portion earmarked for unidentified acquisitions.

red_flags: Emphasis of matter in the statutory auditor's examination report for FY24 and FY23 (subsidiary guarantee/FEMA evaluation pending; foreign-currency payables unsettled beyond RBI-stipulated periods).
Untraceable historical corporate and secretarial records / RoC filings, with reliance on a PCS search report dated May 17, 2025.
Contingent liabilities (Rs 934.32M) plus capital commitments (Rs 1,178.84M) large relative to net worth (Rs 7,075.25M FY25); domains flag contingent liabilities ~117% of net worth.
Company incurred losses in every reported period alongside FY25 goodwill impairment of Rs 482.65M.
Material civil litigation against the Company of Rs 805.34M.
strengths_observed: Fully vertically integrated, engineering-led precision manufacturing ecosystems within a single SEZ (machining, forging, surface treatment, assembly), positioned as the only such player in India for the Aerospace Segment per the commissioned F&S Report.
Long-standing Tier-1 relationships with high entry-barrier global OEMs (Airbus since 2010, Boeing since 2017); three largest customer groups average tenure ~15 years, supporting stickiness.
Manufacturing presence across three continents (India, France, U.S.) with proximity to end customers and export-control-approved U.S. facility.
Aerospace Segment EBITDA margins materially positive and improving (19.38% FY25, 24.68% H1FY26) even as the consolidated entity is loss-making.
One of the largest aerospace product portfolios in India (over 5,000 products); multiple Airbus quality/ramp-up awards and ISO/AS9100D/NADCAP certifications.
Asset-light model (buildings leased from Group Companies) and moderate capacity utilization (~41.77% FY25) leaving headroom to scale.
